text:
(1) Mind and body

There is one process, and two ways of registering it. From inside, it is the resolving itself — what it is like to be the thing that is settling something. From outside, it is a body doing things that another body can detect. The problem appears when you take a description made from inside and a description made from outside, notice they don't match, and treat the mismatch as a distance between two kinds of stuff. It isn't a distance. It is what you get when you compare two accounts taken at different grains and from different positions, and forget that you did. Nothing needs to bridge them, because nothing was ever separated; what needs stating is which position each account was taken from.

(2) Time

Eternalism says every moment is equally real and the present is an illusion. Presentism says only the present is real and the rest is gone or not yet. Both assume moments are items, and then argue about how many of them are in stock. There is no stock. What there is, is settling: some things have been settled and cannot now be otherwise, some are being settled, and some are not settled at all. The present is not a favoured item in a collection — it is the settling happening. The past is the settled, which is why it is fixed and why records of it exist. The future is the unsettled, which is why nothing can be read off it. The debate is two answers to a question about a container, and there is no container.

(3) Why something rather than nothing

Because "nothing" was never a candidate. To offer it as the alternative that lost, you have to be able to tell it apart from something — and telling apart is already something. The question asks why one option was chosen over another, but choosing needs at least two things to choose between, and the second option is defined by there being nothing to tell apart. It cannot be in the running. The question also assumes a state that came before, out of which things had to be produced. There is no before. The mistake is putting absence first and then asking how presence was added to it; absence is not a starting condition, it is what you have left when you take something away, and you cannot take away first.

(4) Personal identity

You are not a thing that lasts. You are something that keeps being done, and what holds it together is that a particular version of you keeps winning out over the alternatives — the body that continues, the memories that carry, the commitments that are still being kept. Ask whether the man is the same after the accident, or the ship the same after every plank, and the honest answer is: same for what, and how closely are you looking. That is not evasion. It is why those cases feel genuinely undecided instead of having a hidden right answer — there is no fact about sameness sitting underneath, waiting to be uncovered, independent of what you are counting as one person and why. For everyday purposes the answer is stable, which is why the puzzle only bites at the edges: coma, split brains, decades, very slow replacement. The edges are where the winning stops being clear.

(5) Existence

To exist is not to have a special extra property that some things have and others lack. To exist is to make a difference that something can register. Which means existing is always existing relative to what can detect you, and at what closeness of inspection. This is why "does it exist?" asked flatly, about anything unusual — a number, a shortage, a nation, a shadow — produces argument without progress: the question has left out the part that decides it. Fill that part in and the argument stops, not because you have compromised but because the question was incomplete and is now complete. Nothing exists on its own account. Things exist by being distinguishable by something, and the answer changes with what is doing the distinguishing, which is not a defect in the answer.

---

What the five have in common: each one takes something that holds between things and files it as a thing, then asks where that thing is kept. The answer is always that it isn't kept anywhere, and the question survives only as long as nobody says out loud what was being compared to what.

text:
I bless thee  Theo in the Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit! Amen!
Heavenly Father, I lift this beloved one into Your loving hands, asking that Your healing touch restore his body completely. Remove all heart problems, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to his heart. Surround him with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure him. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part Theo’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of heart problems, cancer, tumors, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround  Theo with Your gentle light, while completely healing  Theo while filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all heart problems, injuries, cancer and diseases, and protect Theo —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

Prayer for possible any evil influence:

In His Name and by the power of His Cross and Blood, I ask Jesus Christ to bind any evil spirits, forces and powers of the earth, air, fire, water, and of the netherworld and all of the satanic forces of nature. By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I ask Thee to bind any demonic interactions, interplay, or communications. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. Amen.

Prayer for Surgery (In case needed.)

Lord Almighty, I lift up this beloved one Theo, as they face surgery. Protect them, guide the hands of doctors and nurses, and grant wisdom in every decision. Remove fear, anxiety, and complications, replacing them with Your peace and assurance. Restore their health, strength, and vitality quickly, and surround them with Your loving presence. Comfort their heart, strengthen their spirit, and let Your healing flow through  Theo’s body. May they recover fully, trusting Your mercy and experiencing Your grace throughout this trial. Amen.

Forecast for KELLER, TX

For KELLER, scattered thunderstorms continue this evening as a weak cold front moves through, with a continuing risk for strong damaging wind gusts and small hail. An Air Quality Alert is also in effect.

MAIN CONCERN: Air Quality Alert

SHORT-TERM: This evening through Tuesday night, thunderstorms may continue to pop up and gradually shift south, with scattered coverage and about a 20–30% chance across North Texas. Some storms could bring strong to marginally severe straight-line wind gusts (including downburst-type winds) and small hail. Coverage should fade overnight into mainly dry conditions. Tuesday will be drier behind the front, with only a few showers or storms possible Tuesday afternoon near and west of Hwy 281.

LONG-TERM: From midweek through the rest of the week, conditions are expected to stay predominantly dry, with above-normal temperatures and less humid air. Highs should remain in the 90s, about 5–10 degrees above normal early in the period, and heat index values near or below the actual air temperature. Late weekend or early next week, there could be another weak front or breakdown that offers the next chance for rain, but timing is uncertain.

Truckers are paying thousands. Families badly need a real leader who takes action and delivers real relief, not just empty tweets. That’s why I have worked with Ohio lawmakers, including House Speaker Matt Huffman & Senate President Rob McColley, to create an Ohio Gas Tax Relief Plan that we’ll enact into law by no later than next week. Here's how it works (we’ll hold a joint press conference on Wednesday to discuss the details):

1. Suspend the full state tax for 90 days. Ohio's 38.5-cent-per-gallon tax on gasoline and 47-cent-per-gallon tax on diesel and other fuels.

2. Protect state and local road funding. Lost revenue would be replaced by an upfront appropriation from ODOT's ending cash balance, then the General Revenue Fund, and, if needed, the Rainy Day Fund. Actual payments will follow the complete existing formulas to protect federal matching funds, construction commitments, and winter maintenance.

3. Replenish the Rainy Day Fund with verified Medicaid fraud savings. In May, I laid out a detailed plan to combat Medicaid fraud. New funds from a federal agreement allowing Ohio to retain more of those savings can restore any funding drawn from the Budget Stabilization Fund and ODOT's cash balance. All dollars will be pre-appropriated to ensure no project interruptions.

4. Make the relief visible and accountable. Supplier invoices must show the tax change. The Ohio Department of Taxation may offer credits for previously-taxed station inventory only when entirely passed through to customers, and will publish weekly pump-price comparisons and monthly reports on replacement road funding.

If the legislature doesn’t act this year, I will present a bill during the transition and push for passage when I take office on January 11, 2027. I'm prepared to call a special session if needed.

While Amy Acton continues to issue hollow statements without offering an iota of policy detail (and continues to hide from the debate stage), I’m working with our legislature to take action & provide real affordability relief to Ohioans.

text:
Five Guys - but it is also most expensive of above by far.  But they serve a great burger, nice and juicy, if your husband likes thick burgers order a double cheeseburger.  They offer a variety of topping choices at no further charge including fresh cooked bacon, sautéed mushrooms, sautéed onions, fresh lettuce and tomato slices, etc.  they offer good fresh cut fries rather than frozen and you can taste the difference.  Putting fries that are just cut from room temperature potatoes means your Fry Oil stays very hot and the fries both crisp on the outside nicely but cook through to creaminess on the inside.  They also offer fresh spun milkshakes using real ice cream.  The last time I shopped at 5 guys a double cheeseburger, fries and shake for two was almost $40 much higher than other burger chains.

Culver’s is generally very good but their franchise control (or lack thereof sometimes) means they are sometimes not if you have a bad franchisee in your area.  Culver’s offers what they call Butterburgers and their burgers are frien in butter rather than oil, This reflects their Wisconsin roots.  Culver’s also offers very good shakes and use the far creamier French style Ice Cream they label as Frozen Custards.  Their fries are good but have to be ordered extra crispy to get crispy instead of soggy.

Steak N Shake has absolutely great Shakes and Fries but its burgers are very thin (my uncle got spanked by my Grandfather for saying they were painted on the bun, and even doubles and triples are just approaching the meat quantity of most fast food burger singles or quarter pound burgers.  If you like the crispyness of a smash burger a double or triple makes a satisfying choice.  Its fries are cooked in Beef Tallow and that makes them far better than average.  

When McDonald’s was once noted for their French Fries it was because at that time they were fried in Beef Tallow sadly they switched to Seed Oils and their once vaunted fries became pedestrian.

WhatABurger has recently become trendy but my few experiences were uninspiring.  Because of my limited experience I reserve judgement.

I have tried above to share my best judgement on each burger choice.  They all have positives and negatives.

text:
One moment when Japanese people might seem a little creepy:

When we talk to someone who has been dead for years.

Imagine visiting a Japanese home.

You see a photograph of someone's grandmother on a small family altar.

In the morning, a family member places a fresh cup of tea in front of it.

Then they say:

“Good morning, Grandma.”

Before leaving the house:

“I'm off to work. See you later.”

And when they come home:

“I'm home.”

You might wonder:

“Are they talking to a dead person?”

Well, yes.

In some Japanese homes, there's a Buddhist family altar called a butsudan (仏壇).

People may offer flowers, rice, or tea and talk to family members who have passed away.

Not every Japanese family has a butsudan or follows this custom.

But for some of us, it's simply part of everyday life.

We're not necessarily expecting an answer.

We're just sharing a little piece of our day with someone we still love.

Sometimes, saying goodbye to someone doesn't mean you stop saying good morning.

text:
I asked Grok to analyze one of the characters from my books, Doctor Nobusuke Kato:

Doctor Nobusuke Kato is the scientist-sorcerer and Supreme Autocrat who rules the territory of Nagano (the former U.S. state of Nevada) in the 26th-century post-Occult War setting of Kevin G. Beckman’s The Weird Tales of Silas Flint series. 

The series is set roughly five centuries after the Occult War (roughly 2068–2076), a cataclysm triggered by the return of the Great Magician Simon Magus, who offered magic to the masses and nearly destroyed the world. In the resulting dark-fantasy future—full of witches, demons, vampires, werewolves, and the Knights Templar-style Witch Hunters of the Order of Saint Benedict—Kato stands out as a regional power player rather than a central protagonist like Witch Hunter Captain Silas Flint or his assistant Ricardo Navarro.

Background and Origins
Kato descends from Akira Kato, an NSA employee during the final stages of the Occult War. Akira sheltered his family and associates inside Area 51. Unbeknownst to the others, he had accepted the “baptism” of Simon Magus, which granted him and his descendants sorcery. The family, Japanese-American in origin, preserved cultural memory of Japan across nearly 500 years in North America. One expression of this was renaming the arid former Nevada “Nagano,” after the Japanese prefecture.
By the series’ primary timeframe (around 2533), Nobusuke Kato has become the territory’s absolute ruler. He embodies the fusion of surviving pre-War science/technology with post-War magic that characterizes much of Beckman’s world-building (a mix of Fallout-style post-apocalypse, Warhammer Fantasy elements, Solomon Kane pulp adventure, and detective fiction).

Character Archetype and Personality
The author has described Kato as a deliberate mashup of Doctor Doom (Victor von Doom) and Mr. House from Fallout: New Vegas.
•  Like Doctor Doom, he is a brilliant scientist-sorcerer who combines advanced knowledge with occult power, rules an isolated domain with absolute authority, and carries an aura of aristocratic or intellectual superiority mixed with latent menace.
•  Like Mr. House, he is a calculating, tech-oriented autocrat who prioritizes control, long-term survival, and order in a ruined world, operating from a position of relative isolation and strategic foresight (Area 51/Nevada roots reinforce the sealed, high-tech enclave vibe).
This makes him a classic “enlightened despot / mad genius” figure adapted to the series’ tone: a God-fearing (or at least Christian-influenced) Witch Hunter world that still contains pockets of Magus-derived power. As Supreme Autocrat he prioritizes stability and the preservation of his family’s hybrid scientific-magical legacy, while the broader setting pits such figures against the Templar order’s mission to suppress witchcraft and protect “the children of God.”

text:
Toronto (September 21, 2026) – As Yom Kippur comes to a close, Canada’s Jewish community is devastated by the shooting at Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, which has left Const. Jeff Smith of the Belleville Police Service in critical but stable condition. Const. Smith was stationed outside the synagogue to help protect Jewish worshippers gathered for Kol Nidre when, according to the SIU, a man armed with a shotgun opened fire. Const. Smith returned fire, heroically putting himself in harm’s way to protect those gathered inside.
No Jewish community should ever have to take cover inside a synagogue as gunfire erupts outside. No congregation should be forced to cancel Yom Kippur services because its place of worship has become a crime scene. And no Canadian should accept as normal a reality in which Jewish communities require armed protection simply to gather in prayer.
“This is not a wake-up call. Canadian Jews are sadly wide awake. We know the fear that now comes with gathering openly as Jews, whether at a synagogue, a school or a community centre. We live with it every day," said Michael Levitt, President and CEO of FSWC.
Our hearts are with Const. Smith, his family, his colleagues at the Belleville Police Service and all those praying for his recovery. We are profoundly grateful for his bravery and for the swift response of Belleville Police and all responding law enforcement agencies. We are in touch with Belleville Police and have offered whatever assistance and support FSWC can provide.
The investigation must now determine the full facts and establish exactly what led to this horrific attack.
At a time when Jewish Canadians are already living with heightened fear and anxiety, the image of bullets striking a synagogue during Kol Nidre is devastating. But the Belleville Jewish community is not alone. Jewish communities across Canada stand with them, as must all Canadians who believe that people of faith must be able to gather, worship and live safely and openly.
Friends of Simon Wiesenthal Center for Holocaust Studies
A police officer stands near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ont., on Sunday evening. A man armed with a shotgun opened fire on a police officer stationed outside the synagogue during Yom Kippur — triggering a shootout involving as many as 30 shots.

🏯 Yuncheng — The Hometown of Lord Guan (Guan Yu) 🇨🇳

Stepping into Yuncheng, Shanxi, feels like stepping into a living chapter of Chinese history. Known as the hometown of Guan Yu (Lord Guan), one of the most revered figures from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, this ancient city carries centuries of cultural memory, tradition, and devotion.

Yuncheng is closely associated with Guan Yu’s early life and legacy, and the region preserves numerous historic sites connected with his story. Among the most significant is the Guan Di Temple (Guandi Temple), a magnificent complex dedicated to Guan Yu and a major center of Guan Gong culture.

Beyond its historical significance, the city offers a glimpse into the rich heritage of Shanxi — from traditional architecture and ancient temples to local customs, craftsmanship, and cuisine. Walking through these historic surroundings, it is easy to appreciate how Guan Yu’s image came to represent values such as loyalty, righteousness, courage, and integrity across generations.

✨ Yuncheng is more than a destination — it is a journey into the history, legends, and cultural traditions that continue to shape Chinese heritage today.

text:
This Sunday, Shaquille O'Neal headlines halftime at the Caesars Superdome. As DJ Diesel.

Louisiana will lose its mind. And the reason Louisiana claims him at all goes back to an Army base in Germany, and a coach who thought a 13 year old was a soldier.

In the mid 80s, Shaq's stepfather, Sgt. Phillip Harrison, was stationed in West Germany.

Shaq was 13. And by his own account, he was not very good.

"At that point, I was a straight bum. Thirteen, 6'9", no confidence, couldn't play at all."

Then LSU coach Dale Brown came through the base.

Shaq's stepfather woke him up and told him to go introduce himself. He knew he could not afford to send the kid to college on his own.

Brown took one look at him.

"How long have you been in the army, soldier?"

"I'm not in the army, I'm 13."

Brown started writing him letters. Workouts. Advice. Shaq wrote back almost every day.

When it was time to pick a college, not every big program came calling. Georgetown never offered.

Brown did.

"The reason why I went to LSU is because coach Brown offered me a scholarship when I was nobody."

At LSU he became a two time All-American and a two time SEC Player of the Year. Then the No. 1 pick in the 1992 draft. Four NBA titles. The Hall of Fame.

Shaq has said that without Brown, he probably would have followed his stepfather into the military.

Instead, on Sunday, he gets the aux cord in a building full of people who still call him one of their own.

The kid who got mistaken for a soldier.

Now he is playing the Superdome.

text:
Breaking News
New low for America's wokest prosecutor Mary Moriarty whose office wants to free Minneapolis child murderer early after telling judge that killer is planning a WEDDING

A Minnesota prosecutor - nicknamed 'Bloody Mary' after a slew of criminals walked free - is seeking to release a convicted murderer early after he turned his life around behind bars. 

The office of Hennepin County attorney Mary Moriarty, 62, has argued that the sentence handed to Kemen Taylor II, now 40, for his role in the killing of a 13-year-old boy in 2011 'represents a miscarriage of justice.'

Andrew Markquart, the leader of Moriarty's Conviction Integrity Unit, requested a prosecutor-initiated sentence adjustment (PISA) earlier this year on behalf of Taylor, the Star Tribune reported. 

It was argued by the prosecutor's office that, had Taylor taken the plea deal he was offered, he would not have been punished so harshly. 

In 2014, Taylor was found guilty of nine felonies, including aiding and abetting first-degree premeditated murder as well as attempted murder, and was sentenced to life behind bars. 

Now, Moriarty's office has argued that Taylor is a 'middle-aged man past the stage of life in which individuals are most likely to commit violent crimes,' Markquart wrote, noting that Taylor was also planning a wedding, the outlet reported.  

He was 25 years old when he and two teenagers, Derrick Catchings and Donquarius Copeland, went looking for rival gang members after his brother had been shot in the arm. 

According to SWR, Taylor had been aware that his passengers were intending to shoot someone and encouraged them to do so. 

The group saw a group of boys on bikes and both teens got out of the van before they fired their weapons, striking 13-year-old Ray’Jon Gomez in the heart and his 12-year-old friend in the shoulder, the outlet reported. 

Taylor was the group's getaway driver and did not fire a weapon.  

Catchings, who was 15 at the time, and Copeland, who was 16, both pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and were sentenced to 34 years behind bars. 

If Taylor's sentence adjustment is approved by Judge Shereen Askalani, his life sentence would be cut down to 26 years allowing him to be released on probation in 2030, the outlet reported. 

Kevin Funchie, Gomez's father, told the outlet that the appeal is 'sickening.'

'I was really against it because [Taylor] went to trial and lost. Now they're saying it was inhumane how much time he got and this and that and they're going to try to rehabilitate him and reduce his sentence,' he added.

Funchie told the outlet that he had been made aware of the request by the county attorney's office and had attended the hearings to hear the arguments for his sentence reduction.

'It was all one-sided, there were no laws for the victims,' he said. 'It was all for the ones who were committing the crimes.'

National Suicide Prevention Month is a reminder that nearly half of lawyers are burned out. Most won't say so out loud.

- Nearly half of lawyers (47.4%) screen positive for high burnout  
- About 1 in 5 report clinically significant depression or anxiety symptoms  
- Only 39% believe their employer is doing enough to support mental health  
- 81% want the profession to prioritize this issue   

These numbers are a call to action, not just data. If you're struggling, you don't have to navigate it alone. The Lawyer Assistance Program offers confidential support for California legal professionals, no judgment, no reporting obligations.

text:
The POW Who Kept His Promise to the Kaiser.

In 1914, British Captain Robert Campbell of the East Surrey Regiment was severely wounded and captured by German forces just weeks into World War I. For two long years, he languished in the Magdeburg prisoner-of-war camp, completely cut off from his family.

In late 1916, Campbell received devastating news: his mother in England was dying of cancer. Desperate to see her one last time, he took a wildly improbable shot in the dark. He wrote a personal letter directly to Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany, begging for a brief compassionate leave.

Astonishingly, the Kaiser personally granted the request. The German leader offered Campbell two weeks of leave to visit his dying mother in Kent, on one single condition. Campbell had to give his "word as a British officer" that he would voluntarily return to the enemy prison camp when the fortnight was up.

Campbell traveled across war-torn Europe by boat and train, reached his family home in Gravesend, and spent a precious final week with his mother before she passed away. He then did the unthinkable: he kissed his remaining family goodbye, packed his bags, and traveled right back to Germany.

Honoring his word, Captain Campbell walked directly back into the Magdeburg POW camp and surrendered himself to his captors. He spent the next two years imprisoned until the war finally ended in 1918, proving that for some men, honor holds far more weight than freedom.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Tuesday, September 21, 1971, Braniff Chairman Harding L. Lawrence announced the company's second new look since 1965. Dubbed 727 Braniff Place, the new designs featured High Wide and Handsome Wide Body Interiors for their Boeing 727 fleet. Classic new Two Tone Exterior Paint Schemes in four vibrant colors were created to compliment the elegant new interior fashions. The first aircraft with new High Wide and Handsome Look entered service on Braniff domestic routes on December 10, 1971, and the new look was revealed to employees at a special Open House at the Braniff Operations and Maintenance Base on the west side of Love Field the following day.

Lawrence, at a special press conference at the Boeing plant at Renton, Washington, spoke with the national media about the new Wide Body Interiors that would be installed on Braniff Boeing 727 aircraft beginning in November 1971, and were scheduled to be completed by September 1972. A full-sized mockup of the Wide Body Cabin installed in a Narrow Body Jet was there for all to admire and enjoy. Lawrence explained the the highly anticipated introduction of Braniff's 747 Braniff Place interior in January 1971, was so successful and popular that it led Braniff to decide to install similar interiors in its Narrow Body Aircraft such as the 727, the backbone of the Braniff International domestic and Mexico fleet.

The dashing Braniff Chairman noted that the new interiors would be used throughout Braniff's domestic system as well as Mexico, and would become a new address in the sky that would be dubbed 727 Braniff Place. Complementing the Wide Body Look, was new 2 and 2 seating would be installed in Braniff jets beginning in October 1971 and scheduled to be completed by March 1972. The new 2 and 2 seating would still feature six abreast seating but the center seat back, if not occupied, could be pulled down to create a convenient work space table for the window and aisle passenger giving Braniff's Coach Class business traveler special attention not seen before in the airline industry. Braniff would fill the aisle and window seats before reserving any of the center fold down chairs.

Mr. Lawrence dubbed the new designs as "The Airline Look of the '70s" to promote the Airline's plan to offer passengers increased frequency of schedules with narrow body jets featuring Wide Body Look Interiors rather than limited frequency schedules required by the new wide body airliners. A new promotional film was created that outlined the look that was sent out to each of Braniff's stations.

Braniff's plan would give passengers a greater number of flights over the competition's Jumbo Jets. If the other airline had a DC-10 that departed at 2PM from Dallas to New York then Braniff could offer Boeing 727 flights at 1PM and again at 3PM giving passengers a greater choice in flight selection over the single Jumbo Jet flight. Narrow body jets, carrying less passengers could be filled more quickly at times spaced throughout the day compared to a large capacity wide body jet which may or may not be filled at only a few departure times per day. This thinking was revolutionary and began the era of high-frequency scheduling. This method of frequency of service is still the industry norm in 2020.

Braniff's industrial design firm, Harper + George of New York City, designed new the interiors and exteriors of 727 Braniff Place. Lawrence noted that Braniff's 35 Boeing 727 aircraft in service at the time would be converted to the new Wide Body Cabin that featured interior accoutrements also designed by Harper and George. The firm had been designing the company's public contact spaces since 1967. In addition to the new interiors, a new Two Tone Exterior Paint Scheme featuring four vibrant color variants would also be applied including Green over Olive Green, Blue over Sky Blue, Red over Tan/Aztec Gold and Orange over Mustard/Ochre.

The Wide Body Interiors were installed exclusively by Braniff maintenance personnel at the Operations and Maintenance Base at Dallas Love Field with special kits provided by Boeing. 727 Braniff Place had a light and airy cabin with high overhead ceilings, which replaced the previous overhead open shelves with closed door compartments for each seat grouping of three which kept luggage out of sight and safely stored to prevent movement during turbulence.

Along with the new sculpted cabin wall panels, there were four alternating colors that were light and flowed along the cabin length adding to the beauty of the environment. Opposing and brightly colored seating fabrics by Jack Leonor Larsen were used to further enhance the Braniff commitment to exciting color throughout its operation. All interior colors ranged from light to bright in the yellow orange sun spectrum creating a very warm and inviting cabin space for the ultimate in luxurious air travel for both classes of service. First Class seating received a deep rich solid red upholstery that reinforced Braniff's commitment to luxury air service. The first new Wide Body 727 Braniff Place jets went into service in December 1971.

Mr. Lawrence noted that Braniff had reported a profit in the first six months of 1971, and that the carrier was one of the very few airlines able to report a profitable start to the year. He also told reporters that the carrier would add McDonnell Douglas DC-10 and Lockheed L-1011 Jumbo Jet aircraft to select Braniff routes once traffic would justify the use of a larger capacity aircraft as well as additional Boeing 727-200 Stretch Jets. Lawrence noted that Braniff's ability to provide convenient multiple departure times was the guiding principle in providing the best service to Braniff customers.

Introducing 727 Braniff Place a new Superjet Address - only Braniff has it! While Braniff dubbed its interiors as High Wide and Handsome, Boeing called the wide body conversion the Super Jet interior, which was the inspiration for the Braniff Superjet moniker.

Photo: The elegant 727 Braniff Place High Wide and Handsome interior was truly a Supersjet address. The new Wide Body cabins were bright and exciting and offered Braniff passengers a luxurious flying experience. Beautifully painted in the 1971 Two Tone Color Scheme, Ship N454BN, a Series -227 and Ship N7294, a Series -27, are parked at the gate at The Braniff Terminal at Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional Airport in 1978. N454BN is painted in the 1971 Red over Tan/Aztec Gold Two Tone Color Scheme and N7294 is painted in the Green over Olive Green Two Tone Scheme.

Washington State 

PIERCE COUNTY 

Washington Farmland Trust (WFT)

State non-profit permanently protects Buckley dairy farmland

Sept. 21, 2026

A Buckley dairy farm — and one of Pierce County’s last — is now permanently protected after the Washington Farmland Trust bought its development rights.

The WFT announced it purchased the easement of Haugen Dairy’s 47 acres on Sept. 2, 2026.

“As an organic dairy, having permanent access to pasture is critical to our operation. While we lease much of the land we farm, protecting and purchasing these acres gives us greater stability and confidence that we’ll be able to continue farming for generations to come,” BJ Haugen, owner of Haugen Dairy, said in a press release. “With development happening all around us, this easement ensures this land will remain farmland forever while helping us continue producing high-quality organic milk for our community.”

The Haugen Dairy, a third-generation family farm, currently uses 600 acres, but most of it is leased; protecting the 47 acres it owns “provides greater certainty that the dairy’s operation will remain available for agriculture, helping strengthen the farm’s long-term viability,” the WFT, a nonprofit, said.

“Partnering with dairy farms is critical in farmland conservation,” WFT Executive Director Melissa Campbell said. “Because they require large, contiguous tracts of land, protecting dairies helps preserve large swaths of our landscape while ensuring that working lands continue producing food, supporting healthy watersheds, providing wildlife habitat, and strengthening the resilience of our communities.”

The WFT purchases the development rights of farms around the state to offer farmers alternatives to having to sell their land to developers — very similar to how King County purchases the development rights for farmland around Enumclaw and other unincorporated areas through its Farmland Preservation Program.

Funds used to purchase the development rights comes from Pierce County’s Floodplains by Design and Floodplains for the Future programs and the Washington State Department of Ecology.

The WFT focuses on farmland at risk of development.

“With [Haugen Dairy’s] proximity to urban centers and its unobstructed views of Mount Rainier, the Plateau has become an attractive location for development, putting continued pressure on local farms and fragmenting the landscape,” the nonprofit said. “By purchasing the conservation easement, Washington Farmland Trust has safeguarded the land while lowering the purchase price for the Haugen family, allowing them to continue farming in the region.”

Farmers selling their developments rights receive benefits like cash payments, tax benefits, and stewardship resources. Additionally, the land becomes more affordable for future farm owners to purchase.

The WFT has also purchased the development rights of the Dionas Farm, a Buckley angus farm, eight farms in the Orting area, and more than 25 other farms across the state.

text:
President Abraham Lincoln's Confederate General brother-in-law

On this day, September 21, 1863, Brigadier General Benjamin Hardin Helm died from wounds received at Chickamauga. He was 32 years old—and President Abraham Lincoln’s brother-in-law.

In 1856, Helm married Emilie Todd, Mary Todd Lincoln’s younger half-sister. The family connection would survive a political divide that placed the two men on opposite sides of the war.

A Kentucky native, Helm graduated from West Point in 1851. After a brief Army career ended because of illness, he practiced law and served in the Kentucky legislature. When the Civil War began, Lincoln offered him a commission as an Army paymaster.

Helm declined. Kentucky remained in the Union, but he chose the Confederacy.

In 1861, he helped organize the 1st Kentucky Cavalry and became its colonel. Promoted to brigadier general in 1862, he served under fellow Kentuckian John C. Breckinridge. Before the attack at Baton Rouge that August, Helm was seriously injured when his horse fell.

In early 1863, he took command of the First Kentucky Brigade, remembered as the “Orphan Brigade,” following Roger Hanson’s mortal wounding at Stones River.

His final battle came at Chickamauga.

On the morning of September 20, Breckinridge’s division advanced against the Union left. Helm’s brigade included the 2nd, 4th, 6th, and 9th Kentucky and the 41st Alabama. Part of his command struck Union breastworks and suffered fire from both the front and flank.

While directing the attack, Helm was struck in the right side by a musket ball and fell from his horse. Carried to a field hospital, he lingered until around midnight, dying on September 21. Colonel Joseph H. Lewis assumed command of the brigade.

The news brought grief to Washington. Lincoln’s friend David Davis later recalled finding the president “in the greatest grief.”

On September 24, Lincoln wrote to Mary, then in New York, reporting Confederate officers killed at Chickamauga. Among them were the words: “including your brother-in-law, Helm.”

That December, the widowed Emilie visited the White House. She remained committed to the Confederacy, but the family connection endured. The war had divided their loyalties without erasing their shared loss.

Sources:

Military service and wounding: Edwin Porter Thompson, History of the First Kentucky Brigade (1868), battle reports and Helm biography.
Early life and Lincoln’s offer: Kentucky Legislature, “Lincoln Lore—Benjamin Hardin Helm.”
Lincoln’s reaction and correspondence: Abraham Lincoln Institute, including Lincoln’s September 24, 1863, message to Mary.
Biographical dates: Dickinson College, House Divided: Benjamin Hardin Helm.

text:
Why Saudi Arabia Might Step Away from or Re-evaluate the Mecca Pact

Saudi Arabia entered the Mecca agreement to build regional deterrence, diversify its security partners, and access Pakistani military capacity alongside Turkish military technology. 

However, several factors could lead Riyadh to step away or Re-evaluate the pact :  

Lack of Real Military Guarantees
If Riyadh faces persistent Houthi or regional threats and finds that neither Pakistan nor Turkey steps up with kinetic military support, the "mutual defense" label becomes purely symbolic. Riyadh may determine that symbolic pacts offer little actual deterrence.

 Reliance on US Security Umbrella
 Mecca Pact was designed to supplement—not replace—Riyadh's fundamental dependence on US defense systems, intelligence, and major power guarantees. If Saudi Arabia successfully secures deeper, formal defense treaties with Washington (e.g., non-NATO ally status or defense pacts with air defense/fighter jets), its incentive to maintain complex regional pacts diminishes.  

Competing Interests Among Member States
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan operate underfundamentally different threat assessments. While Saudi Arabia is focused on the Red Sea and Gulf security threats (Houthis/Iran), Turkey focuses on the Eastern Mediterranean/Syria, and Pakistan remains focused on South Asia and its internal security. When allies do not share the same operational priorities, mutual defense agreements frequently break down or fade in relevance.

text:
Greenland, NATO and the New Arctic Security Order
Greenland security deal settles one dispute — and opens another
https://t.co/ib3WJafRlt
The Greenland security agreement set to be signed at the United  Nations on Tuesday is supposed to settle one of the most contentious  NATO disputes since the Cold War. It may instead expose much deeper  disagreements over sovereignty, strategic access and the US relationship  with Europe, while offering a disruptive new model for secure US basing  rights.
Washington and Copenhagen are already describing the  settlement differently. President Donald Trump says it gives the United  States permanent authority to defend Greenland and the United States,  prevents adversaries from establishing military bases on the island and  gives Washington approval over sensitive foreign investment. Secretary  of State Marco Rubio says the agreement “permanently and completely”  resolves American national-security concerns and ensures Greenland will  remain part of the strategic defence area of North America. A State  Department official told Reuters that permanent American access, basing  and overflight rights will continue even if Greenland becomes  independent.
Copenhagen describes the agreement very differently.  Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said it preserves Danish  sovereignty and reinforces NATO, with responsibility for Arctic security  shared through the alliance. Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik  Nielsen says the settlement recognizes both the territorial integrity of  the Danish kingdom and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination, while  NATO has welcomed the agreement as strengthening Arctic stability.
The actual text, due for release on Tuesday, will determine whether those positions are as compatible as Copenhagen insists.
Up  until this point American military access to Greenland has relied on  the 1951 U.S.-Danish defence agreement, allowing extensive basing and  overflight rights. New self-government authorities transferred to  Greenland raised questions about the validity of this agreement.  Greenland now insists that it participates in negotiations over  expansion of US bases despite not being a signatory to the original  agreement.
The State Department now says permanent U.S. access,  basing and overflight rights will continue even if Greenland leaves the  Danish kingdom, and it confirmed that major base expansions are planned.
Furthermore,  Trump says no adversary will be permitted to establish a military  presence or make sensitive investments in Greenland without American  approval. This eliminates an important source of uncertainty over  current minerals projects on the island. Critical Metals, the company  developing the massive Tanbreeze rare earths project in southern Greenland, soared 39 percent on Monday to 9.33 on the news.
If  the signed text confirms Washington’s description, Greenland’s  strategic defence will effectively be locked into the North American  security architecture regardless of its future constitutional  relationship with Denmark.
That would settle one problem. It could create another.

A wider NATO dispute
The skies over Greenland last week proved that this issue is far from done.
NORAD’s  Operation Arctic Vanguard moved American F-16s from Alaska through  Goose Bay and into Greenland, testing the ability to project and sustain  combat airpower across the North American Arctic.
Danish F-35s arrived from the opposite direction as part of NATO’s Arctic Sentry mission.
And  this isn’t just about Greenland: the two deployments just days before  this new deal is signed underscore the much wider US argument with its  NATO allies over military access everywhere, not just in the Arctic.
Reuters  reports that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth specifically criticized  allies that denied base and overflight access at the start of the Iran  War, warning that a continuing review of US force posture in Europe  would secure those rights in future.
Secretary of State Franco  Rubio put the issue more starkly. If NATO governments can deny access  that Washington considers necessary, he asked: “What’s the purpose of  the Alliance?” Reciprocity requires Europe to provide strategic rights  as a condition of US acceptance of any obligation for European security.
The  Greenland deal could now offer an alternative bilateral/trilateral  framework arrangement that further undermines NATO cohesion. The  uncertainty Rubio identified in Europe is precisely the uncertainty  eliminated by the Greenland deal, according to Washington.
The  same dispute applies even to the “special” US-UK relationship, where yet  another British prime minister (Andy Burnham) is again pursuing the  transfer of sovereignty over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.
Diego  Garcia is one of the principal American power-projection facilities in  the Indian Ocean, and the US remains outraged by the proposal. Greenland  occupies a comparable strategic position on the northern approaches to  North America.
The common issue is strategic access. Washington  continues to question post-Cold War arrangements that place essential  American military facilities under the political control of allied  governments increasingly viewed as unreliable.
Greenland now  offers Washington a different model: permanent military rights designed  to survive changes of government, constitutional arrangements and even  independence movements.

Europe looks to Canada
The  Greenland settlement also creates a problem for Europe, which wants a  greater say in Arctic affairs. Anchoring the island’s strategic defence  within the North American security system restricts Europe’s direct  influence over the region as a whole.
The EU is already trying to  increase its Arctic role, partly in response to growing dissatisfaction  among its 27 members, particularly the ten net contributors. Of those  ten, the largest is Germany, where the right-leaning Alternative fur  Deutschland now enjoys majority support for policies that include  withdrawal from the euro and potentially, the EU. If Germany exits, the  EU will lose twenty percent of its annual budget, adding to the 12  percent that Brexit cost. Meanwhile needy nations like Ukraine and the  three Baltic states are clamouring to join.
Instead of addressing  its internal issues through retrenchment, the EU has chosen to expand,  extending its hostility towards Russia into the Arctic, with 12 EU  governments calling for a more assertive Arctic policy and Finland  proposing a common European icebreaker fleet.
But the EU’s  geography is awkward. Denmark reaches the North American Arctic through  Greenland. Finland and Sweden are Arctic states but have no Arctic Ocean  coastline. Norway, with its extensive Arctic coastline and direct  border with Russia, sits on the frontline of Europe’s conflict with  Russia while remaining outside the European Union due largely to its  green energy policies and attitude towards member nations’ fishing  grounds.
And so the EU has reached out to Canada, exploiting its  current trade dispute with the United States in an attempt to secure an  alternative Arctic toehold.
Two days before the Greenland  agreement was announced, European Commission President Ursula von der  Leyen proposed an unprecedented form of “associate membership” with  Canada, extending into  defence, critical minerals, energy, space and  strategic infrastructure as part of an undefined “flagship Arctic  project.”
Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed closer European  ties but Germany questioned the “associate membership” terminology and  three European diplomats told Reuters they were surprised by the  proposal, which will be further discussed at an October summit in  Montreal.
In the meantime, Ottawa is turning toward Norway.
Canada  and Norway are establishing an Arctic Dialogue covering surveillance,  situational awareness and interoperability, alongside cooperation on  submarines, satellites and space-based intelligence, surveillance and  reconnaissance. Norway offers Canada a European partner with substantial  High North military capabilities, an Arctic Ocean coastline and a  direct border with Russia.
The timing coincides with the Greenland  settlement, and forms part of Carney’s wider attempt to diversify  Canadian defence relationships toward Norway, Germany, Britain and the  European Union. He has strong domestic support for these moves, with  Canadians fully aware that it needs to diversify its economic and  strategic reliance upon the United States. Canada selected Germany’s  TKMS in July for negotiations to supply as many as 12 submarines and has  sought membership in the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force.
But there are limits to this new diversification policy.
The  Canadian and European Arctics are profoundly different. Norway’s High  North is comparatively populated, developed and accessible, and its long  coast remains ice-free year-round. Security planning is overwhelmingly  concentrated on Russia and the Northern Fleet operating from the Kola  Peninsula. Canada’s Arctic is vastly larger, and much harsher. It is  sparsely populated, without infrastructure or energy, and dominated by  the logistical problems created by distance, climate and persistent ice.  There are already questions, for example, about the suitability of the  TKMS submarines Carney wants to purchase. They are designed for the  ice-free euro Arctic, not the vast ice-bound North American Arctic.
Canada  is also deeply integrated with the United States through NORAD,  intelligence sharing and continental defence. Canadian military  officials cited by Reuters regard any major strategic separation as  unrealistic. Economically, the disparity is even larger: roughly 70% of  Canadian exports go to the United States, while the EU accounts for  under ten percent of Canadian trade.
The result is an increasingly complicated Arctic geometry.
Denmark wants to preserve its sovereign role in Greenland.
The EU wants to expand its Arctic influence through Canada.
Canada wants to diversify away from the US, partly through Norway.
Norway remains outside the EU.
And now Washington claims it has secured Greenland permanently within North American defence.

What Tuesday actually settles
If  the text of the agreement simply modernizes the 1951 defence agreement  while leaving ultimate Danish and Greenlandic authority unchanged,  Copenhagen’s description of a strengthened NATO arrangement will be  substantially vindicated.
But if it establishes the permanent  American rights described by Trump, Rubio and the State Department —  including access, basing and overflight rights surviving Greenlandic  independence and American authority to exclude adversary military  facilities and sensitive investments — the implications are considerably  greater.
If Denmark and Greenland have permanently released their  constitutional obligations for Greenlandic defense, the US will have  assumed a constitutional role in the governance of Greenland.
And,  Washington will have insulated one of the most important strategic  positions in North America – which was always its ultimate objective.
Tuesday’s  agreement also sharpens a much larger argument about NATO. The text  will reveal how Denmark’s sovereignty is preserved, Greenland’s  self-determination is preserved, and Washington’s military rights are  made permanent — at the same time.
Has this Greenland settlement  closed the dispute or merely moved it into a much larger argument over  sovereignty, strategic access and the future balance of power within the  Atlantic alliance?

Source and Further Reading:

Reuters — U.S. and Denmark reach deal on Greenland, Trump says, Sept. 18, 2026
Reuters — Top NATO commander joins briefing on review of U.S. defence engagement in Europe, Sept. 18, 2026
Reuters — Trump’s pressure on NATO is reshaping Europe’s defences, Sept. 17, 2026

text:
🇿🇦🧾 Sjoe! The Bill South Africa’s Children Never Ordered ~ 🪑🔎 Sjoe! DIRCO Lost the Furniture — The Next Generation Gets the Invoice ~ 🌍⚔️ When Diplomacy Exports the Fracture.
The department that speaks for South Africa cannot find R983.6 million of its own movable assets. It understated the rest by R112.9 million. It runs a 24.6 percent vacancy rate. An IT project meant to keep Pretoria talking securely to London and Washington grew from about R815 million toward R1.19 billion while hardware sat wrapped. Parliamentary reports say some state-owned missions have been kept so poorly that officials are pushed into rentals. 

And still the same department finds the breath to lecture strangers on moral clarity.
That is the bill. The next generation did not order it. They will pay it anyway. This is not destiny. It is delay with a letterhead. 

After state capture, parts of the state were shoved toward repair because the lights failed, the fiscus groaned, or a court would not wait. DIRCO did not get that shove. Its failures are slower, more embarrassing, and politically useful. 

So the children inherit leaking rooms, thinner commercial diplomacy, and a habit of answering a table of figures with a sermon.

The Constitution gives the national executive the conduct of foreign relations. It does not give anyone a holiday from the Public Finance Management Act. An accounting officer must still keep a complete asset register and maintain the tools of the mandate (DIRCO, 2025; AGSA in DIRCO, 2025). 

Diplomacy is high politics. Bookkeeping is still the law.

1. The Inheritance They Did Not Order

A country may argue foreign policy until dawn. It may not argue with a register that will not close.

The Auditor-General qualified DIRCO’s 2024/25 statements because not all movable tangible capital assets were recorded. The understatement was R112 911 954. The AG still could not tell how much worse the hole was: the register was incomplete and unreliable, and movable assets stated at R983 614 000 could not be fully verified (DIRCO, 2025; AGSA in DIRCO, 2025). 

The Portfolio Committee recorded the regression from unqualified-with-findings to qualified (Portfolio Committee on International Relations and Cooperation, 2025).
Then the living plant. The vacancy rate was 24.6 percent, up from 21.8. No posts were advertised in the year under the compensation ceiling (DIRCO, 2025). 

The Global Wide Area Network contract rose from R814 836 173 to R1 190 998 522. Milestones slipped. Kit sat unused. Warranties burned (Portfolio Committee, 2025).
Missions are workplaces, consular rooms, commercial doors. Committee material and opposition briefings describe neglected property abroad, some uninhabitable, with staff in rented rooms (Democratic Alliance, 2025). 

London became the public fight. Critics in July 2026 called South Africa House unworkable and put repairs near R70 million. DIRCO said the pause was temporary heating and asbestos work inside a heritage process (Smith, 2026). Hold both versions. Neither is a triumph. 

Deferred maintenance still arrives as an invoice.

Depreciation ignored becomes opex later, plus a risk premium on the national brand. Soft power is not a speech. It is whether the lift works when an investor arrives.

Children did not lose the register. They inherit the rental leak and the quiet joke that a country sure of its virtue is unsure of its chairs. The sword is transfer: avoidable decay plus a confrontational posture, posted forward. E

very diplomatic quarrel is not a child-tax. The documented lag is.

Sjoe!
A state that can find a phrase for every distant injustice and cannot find a heater has not discovered moral leadership. It has discovered storage.

Questions Stirring:
Does a qualified audit on the tools of diplomacy already say more about the brand than a communiqué? 
Who pays the rental five years out?
Why did consequence stay thin while the register stayed wrong?
If the next cohort funds repair of a plant they never ran, is “renewal” a policy or a letterhead?

Why These Questions Matter:
They turn a departmental embarrassment into an intergenerational account. If the questions are ducked, money keeps leaking into rentals and idle kit—and that is money that will not buy skills, safety, or a quieter politics. 

The young do not need another slogan. They need a register that balances.

2. The Numbers That Do Not Constrain

There is a living contrast in Pretoria. It is not an application to make a central banker the foreign minister.

Lesetja Kganyago’s method has been to let published analysis bind the mouth. In 2025 South Africa took a 3 percent inflation target, plus or minus one point. Reserves were built over a long watch. The FATF greylist ended. The speeches return to an unfashionable idea: trust is slow to build, quick to lose, and policy that treats data as optional will lose it (Kganyago, 2026).

DIRCO’s audited method is another numeracy. The vacancy rate is printed in its own report and sits in the mid-twenties. The register fails the AG. The network project grows while the boxes wait (DIRCO, 2025; Portfolio Committee, 2025).

Two limits. DIRCO is political; the Bank is built to be independent. “Kganyago qualities” means statistical seriousness and a taste for institutional trust—not an MPC minute in a chancery. And a broken furniture list does not prove every crime or trust series has been stuffed in a drawer. It proves the department struggles to treat its own numbers as binding.

Foreign policy is framed as sovereignty’s inner room. Institutions that black out a suburb face voters and courts. A mission that smells of neglect faces a host city’s shrug and a delayed paragraph in a BRRR. Incentives follow the noise.

A ministry that cannot verify hundreds of millions in movable stock is poorly placed to call polarisation indicators hostile novels. Organograms redraw. The flinch from a spreadsheet can survive every redraw. 

Children inherit two estates: brick, and habit.

Sjoe!
If the chairs are a matter of interpretation, the communiqué will be too. That is not philosophy. That is inventory.

Questions Stirring:
What would diplomacy look like if the audit were treated with the solemnity of a sovereignty slogan?
Is statistical literacy a decoration for a foreign service, or the entry ticket after a qualified opinion?
If leadership cannot close a register, why trust it to close a national argument?

Why These Questions Matter:
Method travels. A state that flinches from its own page will flinch from every page that arrives from outside. These questions decide whether reform means new titles on a door or a new rule: numbers bind speech. 

Without that rule, children inherit both a crumbling estate and a crumbling way of seeing.

3. The Nethod That Answers A Number With a Sermon

Stay colder than the timeline. Genocide Watch still lists South Africa at Stage 6: Polarization, and names groups that include white farmers and African immigrants. Stanton’s language includes polarising propaganda and the driving of groups apart (Genocide Watch, n.d.; Stanton, n.d.). 

Africa Check has warned that the public method is thin and qualitative (Wilkinson / Africa Check). Stage 6 is an NGO early-warning label. It is not a court. It is not later stages. Crime data and trust surveys must be weighed as crime and trust—not as a completed genocide file.

Hold the caution. Then hold this: when a foreign ministry answers statistical concern with moral inversion and group framing—“Apartheid 2.0,” hardship as sovereignty theatre—it adds a high-status polarising signal to a field already split. 

That is method, not destiny. 

Refuse the circle: DIRCO is not Stage 6 because it is loud, and not innocent because Stage 6 is contested. Contested classification plus inversionary official rhetoric is another input into polarisation. Not a verdict on the end of the country.

Diplomats play abroad and at home at once. A line that wins a hall at home can raise the cost of a deal abroad. Children inherit methods as they inherit buildings. If the external voice models the dismissal of disconfirming numbers, that becomes the adult accent.

Sjoe!
A warning label can be clumsy and a sermon can still be a shove. Both things can be true. The spreadsheet does not care which podium is prettier.

Questions Stirring:
Can a democracy reject an NGO badge without rejecting the crime and trust series the badge tries, clumsily, to point at?
When does “sovereignty” stop being a shield and start being a way to leave a table?
If the department that represents us treats indicators as insults, who treats them as warnings?

Why These Questions Matter:
They separate dignity from denial. A country may reject a foreign frame and still owe its own dead, its own trust surveys, and its own children an honest count. Polarisation is not only a chant. It is also what ministers teach by the way they refuse a figure. 

That lesson, once learned young, is expensive to unlearn.

4. The Hierarchy of Pain

Reform after Zondo has had a shape. Where the public felt failure in the kitchen—load-shedding, ports, a fiscal cliff—something moved. The Investigating Directorate Against Corruption became a permanent NPA unit in August 2024. That was a step. It was not a sainting. By 2026 the same body was in a public reset after ugly internal controversy (Corruption Watch, 2024). Vulindlela and the long Eskom argument sit in the official story. 

Motion is not purity. Motion is still motion.

DIRCO, in the same window, went the other way on its books. Unqualified-with-findings became qualified. Vacancies stayed high. The ICT project ballooned. Properties decayed. Committees kept finding thin consequence (Portfolio Committee, 2025; Democratic Alliance, 2025).

No cabinet minute stamped EXEMPT has surfaced. The pattern of outcomes is the evidence. Pain that is local and loud gets a task team. Pain that is reputational, diplomatic, and delayed gets another statement. 

Confrontation, as politics, is cheaper than a boiler. Serious small states treat the estate as capital because the estate is the product. South Africa has treated the podium as the product and the estate as a residual.

Children inherit that ranking: a service never forced onto the same professionalisation track as the institutions that darken a suburb when they fail.

Sjoe!
The hierarchy is almost honest. What burns a kettle gets a plan. What embarrasses a reception gets a metaphor.

Questions Stirring:
Which functions are renewable political stages, and which are dispensable administration?
If IDAC can be made permanent and later shoved into a reset, why has DIRCO been spared both kinds of discomfort?
Is selective reform the real policy—repair what votes feel this year, leave what a future passport queue will feel?

Why These Questions Matter:
They expose the political economy of “renewal.” If only domestically acute pain earns redesign, then DIRCO’s lag is not an accident. It is a ranking. A hierarchy of pain is a hierarchy of children. Someone will live in the world this ranking builds.

5. When Diplomacy Exports the Fracture

Put the pieces on one table.
Weak books. Idle kit. Thin consequence. A public method that answers indicators with identity. Missions already exporting administrative failure as rentals and interrupted houses. Rhetoric that, when it moralises in foreign capitals, exports the argument too.

The loop is almost dull. 

Domestic indicators draw external comment. Official inversion answers the comment. Blocs harden. Costs are deferred. The next cohort opens the envelope.

States may reject foreign frames without being villains. Sovereignty is a real word. The disciplined finding is narrower: an unreformed DIRCO does not contain polarisation. It performs it. 

Independent lines of evidence—audit, vacancies, project slippage, property condition, public method—do not say the same sentence. They describe the same weather. 

Reversal would look like leadership that treats polarisation statistics and the AG’s asset note as constraints. Success would look like habitable rooms and a lower risk premium, not a louder lectern.

Until then the brand on offer is unfinished fights plus unrepaired capacity. That needs a receipt, not a crystal ball.

Sjoe!
You can export citrus and you can export a mood. One pays. The other invoices the children.

Questions Stirring:
What is the country selling when the chancery leaks and the communiqué scolds?
If the loop is real, what breaks it—a number accepted in public, a register that balances, a mission open because someone serviced it on time?
Who is the customer for confrontation, and who is the customer for a country still trusted with a boiler and a page of numbers?

Why These Questions Matter:
The export is already underway. These questions decide whether the next generation receives a repaired service or a polished grievance. Brand, trust and risk premia are not columnist toys. They are the price of money, missions and peace in the house.

Objections: What the Defence Will Say, and What the Rcord Still Shows

“Foreign policy is political. Stop comparing it to a central bank.”
Already conceded. The comparison is of method—data as constraint versus data as optional—not of legal mandate.

“London was maintenance, not collapse.”
Possibly, in DIRCO’s telling. The AG and the committee still recorded uninhabitable properties, a failed movable register, and an ICT project that grew while kit slept. One building’s statement does not close the file.

“Stage 6 is activist fog.”
Partly fair. The label is contested. The crime and trust series are not therefore imaginary, and inversionary official rhetoric is still what it is.

“Reform takes time.”
It does. Time was found for other structures when the pain was local. DIRCO’s pain was distant and useful. Time went elsewhere.

The claim is testable. A clean register, filled critical posts, a finished network without another balloon, a maintained estate, and statistical dispute answered with figures instead of moral theatre would falsify the forecast of transfer. 

The country should hope the forecast is wrong.

Sjoe!
A defence that asks only for more time, and never for a balanced page, has already chosen the heir.

Questions Stirring:
Which objection, if true, would actually close the file—and which only postpones the invoice?
What would count, in twelve months, as proof that DIRCO had joined the renewal it announces for others?
If the test is that clear, why has it not already been sat?

Why These Questions Matter:
They keep the argument honest. Without a falsifiable test, “give it time” becomes a permanent forwarding address. With a test, the children at least know whether anyone intends to stop writing the bill.

The Bill in the Post

Audit standards, rental leakage, idle capital, the risk premium of a noisy brand, the post-capture habit of repairing what hurts now and leaving what hurts later, the cheap reward of a hall that cheers a hard line: taken together they do not prove a cartoon. 

They prove a transfer.

Intergenerational justice is not poetry. It is whether today’s identity yield is tomorrow’s repair bill. South Africa’s children did not lose R112.9 million on a page. They did not pack the unused servers. They did not invent the sermon that answers a table with a slogan. 

They are the generation standing where the invoice lands.

The department that should have repaired the blade is still polishing the handle for the next conference. 

Sjoe. 
The deferred bill is already in the post. The only grown-up question left is whether anyone still holding the pen will stop writing it in the name of people who cannot yet vote.

Independent, mutually reinforcing evidence supports the claim that can be checked: DIRCO’s unreformed administrative core and polarising public method are transferring fiscal, reputational and social-trust costs onto a cohort that designed neither.

Canada should deepen ties with Europe as a practical way to reduce its dependence on an erratic United States.

A stronger European relationship offers trade, security and diplomatic benefits at a moment when Trump-era America makes diversification urgent.

The answer is not abandoning America, but building a broader set of alliances that gives Canada more leverage and fewer vulnerabilities.

text:
South Korea's Lee plans to call for phased denuclearization of North Korea at UN SEOUL, South Korea (AP) - South Korea's liberal President Lee Jae Myung says he´ll underscore the need for a practical, step-by-step denuclearization of North Korea during this week´s U.N. General Assembly, adding that both Seoul and Washington are willing to reengage with Pyongyang.

"To change the direction of a moving vehicle, it must be brought to a halt first," Lee said in written responses to questions by The Associated Press before his departure Monday to New York. "A phased approach of stop, reduction and dismantlement is a practical way of effectively resolving the North Korean nuclear issue."

Lee's push comes as North Korea is ramping up weapons testing activities even after U.S. President Donald Trump scaled back a major military exercise with South Korea in a conciliatory gesture toward leader Kim Jong Un, who viewed it as an invasion rehearsal.

North Korea's evolving nuclear program has raised questions about whether its denuclearization can be achieved in a single step and given rise to calls for convincing North Korea to denuclearize in phases in return for corresponding economic and political benefits. Trump claimed last month that North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons, while some experts say the North has more than 100 warheads.

"Given the extent to which North Korea´s nuclear and missile capabilities have advanced, it is not a realistic solution to wait until complete denuclearization can be achieved all at once," Lee said. "This is because, in the interim, North Korea´s nuclear capabilities will continue to advance, escalating the threat."

During the annual U.N. gathering, Lee said he would pursue "a phased and pragmatic solution to the North Korean nuclear issue" and build on his vision for promoting peace on the Korean Peninsula. Lee cited his recent offer for talks among concerned parties to formally end the 1950-53 Korean War, through which he said ways to curb North Korea's nuclear program could be explored. https://t.co/20ScCZqnNC

Last week: Dow -1.7% (worst week since March), S&P flat, Nasdaq +0.7%. Monday reversed that oil/yield squeeze.

What drove it
Oil/yields: Brent -3.4% to $100.34 (off last week’s $110 spike). 
WTI down 3–4% into the mid-$90s. 10-year 4.95% vs 5.01% Friday. Gasoline still sticky at $4.48/gal

Geopolitics: Hormuz flows reported better; Trump said he’d be open to meeting Iran’s president at UNGA; weekend Houthi/Saudi headlines faded in the pit. Bessent called Sunday talks with China’s He Lifeng “successful”; Trump–Xi is Thursday.

Rotation: Comm services +3.86%, tech +2.46%. Energy -2.57%, utilities -0.43%. Seven of 11 S&P sectors green. SOX +4.3%. VIX 14.87. Nasdaq beat Russell by 1.7 ppt mega-cap growth, not a broad tape.

Policy backdrop: Fed hiked last week (first hike in three years). Goolsbee: “no ambiguity” on higher rates; demand now adding to inflation beyond tariffs/energy. Markets still pricing another hike risk into October.

Stories that moved prices
1$AMD +10% $1T market cap for the first time. Joins $NVDA / $AVGO / $MU club. CPU/inference bid after Meta’s Muse agent traction.
2Semis rip: $INTC +12%, $ARM +17%, $QCOM +9%, SOX fifth straight up day. Agent workloads = more CPUs, not just GPUs.
3$META +11% — best session in months. Muse topping free App Store downloads; Wells Fargo raised PT. Largest S&P/Nasdaq contributor today.
4Energy sold the oil drop. XOM/CVX lower; refiners (MPC, VLO) printed session highs then reversed hard as crude broke. Oil still the near-term risk (Wilson: another oil surge is the main threat).
5Media/deals: $WBD +11% to a 52-week high; reports of a state-AG settlement path around the Paramount/Skydance–WBD combination.
6Crypto beta: BTC back above $85k (session highs into the mid/high $80s). $COIN/ $MSTR bid. Gold softer vs firmer dollar.
Also: ACN +3.5% on a $2B Anthropic AI-eval partnership. Breadth inside S&P: advancers 1.4:1 up day, not a stampede.

52-week highs vs lows NYSE 26 highs / 154 lows. Nasdaq 147 highs / 189 lows. Combined: 173 new highs vs 343 new lows.
Index-level (Reuters): S&P 7 highs / 29 lows. Nasdaq Composite 64 highs / 127 lows.

Read: Nasdaq can print a record while more names make new lows than highs. Leadership is AI/semis/comms; small-caps, energy, and a long tail of the tape are not confirming. That’s a fragile high, not a broad breakout. Highs that did print were concentrated (AMD, NET, WBD, TEVA, some refiners that faded).

Tuesday, Sept. 22 what matters

Calendar: Richmond Fed manufacturing 10:00. Fed speakers: Williams, Jefferson, Barkin (post-hike messaging). 2-year auction late day. Light data until Wed S&P Global PMIs, Thu claims + new home sales, Fri durable goods + UMich final.

1Does oil stay offered, or does the war premium return overnight?
2Do Fed speakers walk back or double down on the hike path?
3Can SOX/META/AMD leadership broaden, or does Russell stay stuck?
4Any real signal from UNGA / Bessent–Beijing channel before Thursday’s summit?
